messages:
olivia: Incident bot fired: high error rate on smart-routing fallback policy for customer 'finserv-xyz'. Seeing a surge of region fallback loops and 5xx from rdw-v2 variants. Paging SREs.
incident-bot: HIGH-PRIORITY: routing-policy:smart-routing -> 503 spike, 90th latency > 1.5s, affected region: us-west-2 -> panic fallback triggered. Pagerduty incident created: PD-4281.
sre-oncall: I'm on it. Can someone dump recent policy changes?
mike: I rolled a change to fallback thresholds ~10m ago (lowered success threshold from 0.8 -> 0.6) to reduce cold-starts. I also added a new mapping for model alias `rdw-v2` -> `rdw-v2-quant` on us-west-2 to save cost.
olivia: can we correlate the timing with customer errors? product-lead: finserv-xyz reported timeouts starting ~1750001200 in support thread.
nyt: (bot noise) ignore
nina: I'm joining. If fallback policy is too aggressive it'll force region swaps; combined with the alias mapping we might be routing to the wrong model variant that is incompatible with existing KV cache.
tzeng: Confirmed logs: routing-service shows repeated region-select decisions every ~60s per session for some customers -> loop behavior (us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 -> us-west-2).
mike: hmm, I did allow cross-region fallback for that alias in the policy. My intent was to increase availability, not loop.
sre-oncall: This is causing session KV cache mismatches and grpc errors from the runtime: "incompatible-kv-format" in rdw-v2-quant. That explains the 5xx.
olivia: customer impact: moderate for finserv-xyz, some calls failing, but many customers unaffected. We should assess blast radius. product-lead: finserv-xyz on Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 — high priority.
incident-bot: HANDOFF: oncall -> olivia at 1750001250.
olivia: I'm going to try a manual override to pin model variant and region for that customer while we rollback the policy. Plan: force-region us-west-2 and force-model rdw-v2 (non-quant) for customer 'finserv-xyz'. Any objections?
mike: if you force rdw-v2 we might hit capacity; non-quant uses more GPU memory. We need to check capacity before forcing.
sre-oncall: agree check. Current pod utilization in us-west-2 is 72% for dedicated pool; should fit a pinned session but bursts could happen.
nina: caution: last time a force-model override was applied it bypassed the routing cache invalidation and caused stale session tokens to be replayed. Make sure to run a cache flush for that customer.
olivia: noted. Steps: (1) create temporary policy override for the customer, (2) flush KV cache for customer, (3) monitor error rate, (4) rollback policy change.

---

olivia: executing override: 
```
# admin-cli
redwood override set --customer finserv-xyz --region us-west-2 --model rdw-v2 --ttl 600
```

olivia: manual override applied. Now flushing KV cache:
```
redwood cache flush --customer finserv-xyz --type kv
```

olivia: cache flush returned 200 OK. Watching logs.

(2 minutes pass)

mike: I'm seeing a drop in 5xx for that customer but overall routing-service still shows fallback churn for other customers.
olivia: good for finserv-xyz. Error rate for that tenant down to baseline.

(10 minutes pass)

sre-oncall: Uh — noticed a spike in latency for other Dedicated tenants in us-west-2 at 1750001345. Tracing shows many sessions suddenly pinned to non-quant rdw-v2 -> memory pressure -> evictions -> OOMs in a few xg instances.
mike: oh no. The override must have influenced placement decisions across the pool due to scheduler affinity tweaks. I didn't expect cross-tenant scheduling effects.
nina: this is the exact side-effect I warned about: cross-tenant rollback/override causing capacity imbalance and unexpected evictions.

product-lead: customer impact update: two mid-market customers in us-west-2 experienced degraded latency. We should escalate to SEs.

olivia: reverting override to avoid further OOMs. Running:
```
redwood override delete --customer finserv-xyz --region us-west-2 --model rdw-v2
```

mike: also I'm starting an emergency rollback of the mapping and the fallback threshold change from earlier. Rolling back mapping alias and threshold.

(5 minutes pass)

incident-bot: ROLLBACK_COMPLETED: mapping alias & fallback threshold restored to previous version at 1750001375.
sre-oncall: After rollback, OOM rate dropped and latency is returning to normal. However, we still have some leftover session state pointing to rdw-v2 on a few nodes. Need a targeted cleanup.
nina: propose running targeted session eviction for customers with stale session KV:
```
redwood sessions evict --filter "model:rdw-v2" --limit 50
```

olivia: queued session eviction. Monitoring.

(10 minutes)

olivia: All metrics stabilizing. finserv-xyz back to normal and other tenants recovered. Root cause summary draft: unintended interaction of a recent policy change (lowered fallback success threshold) + alias mapping of `rdw-v2` -> `rdw-v2-quant` allowed cross-region fallbacks which, for some session patterns, triggered region flip-flopping. Manual override to pin model/region temporarily fixed the customer symptom but introduced capacity pressure and evictions because it bypassed scheduling safeguards and didn't invalidate all session caches gracefully.

mike: action items: 1) revert alias mapping in policy to prevent cross-region routing for variant aliases (done), 2) add a preflight capacity check to manual override flow, 3) ensure override triggers session cache invalidation automatically, 4) add a safety throttle to prevent cross-tenant scheduling shifts when a single tenant is pinned.
sre-oncall: I'll open PD follow-ups for the OOMs and schedule a post-incident review.
product-lead: communicate to affected customers with timeline and mitigation steps.
olivia: thanks everyone. Marking incident as mitigated but we keep PD open for postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED at 1750001398.
mike: quick note — let's document the override CLI behavior and capacity checks in Runbook. I'll take that.
nina: I'll draft the postmortem including reproducible traces and suggested config safeguards.
olivia: handoff to follow-up owners: mike (override runbook), nina (postmortem), sre-oncall (PD follow-ups).
product-lead: thumbs up.
olivia: closing thread soon, leaving logs for audit. :white_check_mark:
